title.en: Memory allocation: one first-fit fragmentation trace

summary: Replay one address-ordered heap so allocation failure, internal waste and external holes remain distinct.
objective: Build a bounded contiguous-heap trace where aligned first-fit allocations split free blocks, frees coalesce adjacent blocks, and a request can fail despite enough total free bytes.
intent_signals: show first fit split and coalesce
request fails despite enough free memory
example_prompts: Replay a 64-byte first-fit heap: allocate 9,16,16,16 bytes, free selected blocks, show a 24-byte failure, then coalesce and retry.
negative_signals: Not virtual memory, paging, garbage collection, compaction, concurrency, production malloc metadata, performance comparison or a general allocator simulator.
not_for: No heap growth, relocation, compaction, thread safety, headers/boundary tags, best-fit/buddy/slab policy or claimed real allocator performance.

entities.name: Addressed heap rail
entities.guidance: Blender constructs a 64-cell or proportionally segmented rail with sturdy allocation blocks and removable ownership tags. Three.js owns byte intervals and positions pieces from exact addresses, never from physics.

entities.name: Trace and metrics
entities.guidance: Show ordered free intervals, requested versus charged size, internal waste, total free bytes and largest hole at every committed step. A failed request remains in the trace without mutating the heap.

state_contract.model: One fixed contiguous half-open heap [0,64), 8-byte alignment, no headers, relocation, growth or compaction. Blocks are disjoint half-open intervals labeled free or allocated(owner,requested,charged); charged=ceil(requested/8)*8. The free list is address ordered. allocate(owner,n) rejects duplicate owner, n<=0 and overflow; it chooses the lowest-address free interval with length >= charged, allocates its prefix and preserves any remainder. free(owner) rejects unknown/double free and then repeatedly coalesces exactly adjacent free neighbors. Preset: allocate A=9 -> [0,16) with 7 internal bytes; B=16 -> [16,32); C=16 -> [32,48); D=16 -> [48,64). Free B and D: total free=32, largest hole=16, so E=24 fails from external fragmentation. Free C coalesces [16,64), then E=24 succeeds at [16,40).
state_contract.authority: Three.js owns intervals, ordering, arithmetic, trace snapshots and error states. Blender-authored blocks are visual identities whose transforms derive from addresses.
actions: Allocate the next preset owner or enter a positive request; preview aligned charged size before commit.
Free one allocated owner and inspect each adjacent coalescing result as one committed operation.
Step backward/forward through immutable snapshots; reset restores one [0,64) free interval.
Compare total-free and largest-hole values at the failed and successful E requests.

invariants: Sorted blocks partition [0,64) exactly: no gaps, overlap or zero-length interval; allocated plus free charged bytes always total 64.
Internal fragmentation is sum(charged-requested) inside allocated blocks. External fragmentation is represented by separated free intervals; total free alone does not imply a request fits.
First fit chooses the lowest-address adequate free interval in this address-ordered model and splits only when a positive remainder exists.
Free coalesces all directly adjacent free intervals. Invalid allocate/free actions and failed fit leave state and history unchanged except for a visible error result.
motion_guidance: Step commits one discrete semantic action; pause freezes playback without changing committed state. Reset cancels pending animation and restores the complete preset, including clock, history, selection and error state.
Use a static before/after view and readable tables for reduced motion. Camera movement and token/message travel only explain a committed transition.
creative_affordances: Blender may shape distinctive, stable parts and materials for the chosen metaphor; Three.js binds those parts to model IDs and derives every label, highlight and transform from semantic state. Color is reinforced with text, shape or pattern.
The layout may be sculptural, planar or spatial, provided ordering, identity and invalid states remain unambiguous.
known_limits: One deliberately small pedagogical trace with fixed alignment and excluded metadata; it does not characterize a production allocator or compare policy performance.
Authored, source-reviewed guidance only; no Blender export, solver, allocator, TLS stack, browser, renderer or interactive artifact was run.

physical_contract.scope: Heap blocks are exact address intervals; apparent packing/contact and animated movement do not allocate memory.

object_craft.structure: Use a fixed engraved address bed, flush interval blocks and separate owner/request/charged tags. Preserve a visible hairline at every exact boundary and an unambiguous failed-request staging slot.
object_craft.material: Allocated owners use distinct patterns plus letters; free holes share one neutral material, while internal waste uses a hatch inside its allocated block.

claims.statement: Unused capacity inside an allocated unit larger than requested is internal fragmentation; free capacity split among separate holes is external fragmentation. A simple allocator may manage a fixed contiguous byte region without relocation or compaction.
claims.scope: The chapter’s simplified free-space-management model and this recipe’s explicit fixed-heap specialization.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 17, PDF pages 3–4 (PDF indices 1–2): internal/external fragmentation, no relocation and fixed contiguous region

claims.statement: First fit chooses the first sufficiently large free block and keeps the remainder free; address-ordered free lists make adjacent coalescing easier, and freeing neighboring chunks permits them to merge.
claims.scope: Address-ordered first fit with splitting and immediate coalescing; no performance guarantee.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 17, PDF page 5 and pages 12–13 (PDF indices 3, 10–11): coalescing and First Fit
